A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNIP research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original infrared segmentation benchmarks, UNIP experiments, and ablations, including Table 4 and the supplementary experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including UNIP fine-tuning and linear-probing outcomes in Table 4 and the Appendix E experiments.

M1.justification: NMI-HAD, InfMix construction, LL-FPN, and head alignment are unchanged. Equation (2) replaces H/h with M/m for attention heads without changing the KL loss or distillation procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same InfMix pre-training data, SODA/MFNet-T/SCUT-Seg benchmarks, and RGB/depth probing evaluations in Table 10. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The six pre-training baselines in Table 11 and segmentation comparators in Table 5 are unchanged. Feature-distillation and continual-pre-training comparisons in Tables 6 and 9 also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures, dataset splits, preprocessing, model sizes, training schedules, and hyperparameters remain identical in Sections 2 and 4 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: Both contain the same attention and CKA analyses, distillation-layer and hyperparameter studies, LL-FPN ablations, and dataset analyses. Appendix E retains the same data-scaling, training-strategy, multi-layer, and head-wise distillation experiments.

E5.justification: Point-estimate and correlation reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests that distinguish it from the other.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings remain unchanged, including the appendices. For example, Table 4 reports the same 64.37 average FT and 44.04 average LP for UNIP-S distilled from MAE-L.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1, Equation (12), repairs a mismatched summation index: v1 sums NMI^m over h, whereas v2 correctly sums over m and uses M as the head count. This locally corrects the written head-average definition; the surrounding derivation and limiting cases are unchanged. Equation (2) otherwise only renames notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions, hybrid-attention claim, UNIP components, performance and efficiency claims, and proposed applicability beyond infrared.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning hybrid attention, texture bias, and distribution shift are unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitation that UNIP itself is validated only for infrared semantic segmentation and proposes extensions to other modalities and tasks.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, head-alignment instructions, and dataset construction procedures in Appendices C and F are unchanged. The documented code link and other external link destinations also remain identical.

R1.justification: Appendix A, the reference list, and comparisons with prior research are unchanged. No cited work or novelty positioning is added or removed.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to attention-head notation in Equations (2) and (12) and the arXiv version/date stamp. Prose, headings, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation (2)'s number moves onto a separate line, with small surrounding spacing changes on pages 7 and 21. No figure or table is added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the inconsistent summation index in Equation (12) and standardizes attention-head notation across the mathematical specification. This provides a limited clarity and correctness improvement; methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
